app.title: FCS-Protein Oligomerization Simulator
app.summary: The person picks an oligomerization equilibrium model (dimer, trimer, or tetramer through a dimer intermediate). They enter the dissociation constant(s), the labelling efficiency, the labelled-protein concentration and a total-concentration range. Then they run the simulation. The interface computes the predicted normalised apparent diffusion time and the fraction of protein in each species across a log-spaced concentration titration, draws both as stacked curves, and offers the simulated values as a CSV download.

task.text: Predict how a fluorescence correlation spectroscopy titration should look for a chosen oligomerization model and set of constants, so the person can plan or interpret a concentration series.

data.text: No input data. Model parameters typed in by the person produce simulated curves: an apparent diffusion time and species fractions, each computed at log-spaced total concentrations.
data.item: one total-concentration point on a simulated titration curve

stage.text: planning a concentration titration and interpreting FCS measurements against binding models

mechanism.text: A sidebar form holds the model choice, constants and concentration range, and shows each model's equations as typeset formulas. Running it recomputes a two-panel figure in the main area: apparent diffusion time over concentration, with a second axis in monomer units, above the species fractions. A download button exports the same values.

field.text: oligomerization equilibrium modelling for fluorescence correlation spectroscopy in biophysical chemistry

workflow.name: simulate a model's response curve from chosen parameters and export it

steps.here: Run Simulation solves the equilibrium on 200 log-spaced concentrations, using polynomial roots for the tetramer, to get the normalised τapp and each species' fraction
stacked log-x plots: τapp/τn with a secondary monomer-concentration axis on top, and fractional concentration for each species with a legend below
Download CSV saves concentration, normalised τapp and the species fractions under a grouped header, named after the model

distinctive: The apparent diffusion time is weighted by brightness: labelling efficiency and labelled-protein concentration change how much each species counts
Fixed diffusion-time ratios between species (0.79 per doubling, 0.69 for a trimer) are built into each model
A twin x-axis converts oligomer-unit concentration into total monomer concentration
The trimer is set by an effective dissociation constant derived from the true Kd
Changing the model refreshes the plots live; changing any other parameter needs an explicit run
